body.statement: The function \(\delta\mapsto P_\delta(a)\) is constant on every open component of \(\mathbb R\setminus\mathcal B(a)\), while a singleton breakpoint may have a distinct equality-face value. Since \(|\mathcal B(a)|\le n^2\), \(\mathsf{Invert}\) returns the complete, possibly disconnected confidence set \(\mathcal I_\alpha(a)\), including exact endpoint status, with \(O(n^2)\) calls to \(\mathsf{ChamberMax}\).
body.justification: Finite equality-aware inversion replaces a grid and does not assume a monotone or connected p-value curve.
body.gap: Luo et al. give careful Fisher inversion and Caughey et al. use effect-increasing ranks, but neither handles optimizer changes caused by an attrition envelope on a weighted support.
body.consumer: Applied researchers obtain every accepted additive effect and its correct open or closed boundary.
body.proof_tex:
Fix the realized assignment and observation indicators.  For an observed treated unit \(i\), its sharp-null baseline coordinate as a function of the hypothesized effect is
\[
x_i(\delta)=Y_i(1)-\delta,
\]
whereas for an observed control \(j\), it is \(x_j(\delta)=Y_j(0)\).  Two observed coordinates in the same treatment arm have a difference independent of \(\delta\).  An observed treated coordinate and an observed control coordinate are equal exactly when
\[
\delta=Y_i(a_i)-Y_j(a_j).
\]
Thus all possible changes in the ordered equality-block partition of the observed labels occur in \(\mathcal B(a)\), by its definition.

Let \(J\) be an open component of \(\mathbb R\setminus\mathcal B(a)\).  Every pairwise sign \(\operatorname{sgn}\{x_i(\delta)-x_j(\delta)\}\) is constant for \(\delta\in J\): this is immediate for same-arm pairs, and for a cross-arm pair its sole zero, if any, is a breakpoint not in \(J\).  Hence the observed ordered partition is constant throughout \(J\).  The compatible complete weak orders are exactly the total preorders extending that observed partition, so the set \(\mathfrak W_\delta(a)\), viewed as a set of ordered label partitions, is also constant on \(J\).  For any one such partition, its midrank vector and all design-row tail indicators depend only on block membership and block order, not on the numerical values representing the blocks.  The weak-order maximum formula therefore proves that \(P_\delta(a)\) is constant on \(J\).

At a breakpoint, one or more treated and control observed blocks can merge.  The compatible weak-order complex at that singleton can consequently differ from both adjacent complexes, so its value must be evaluated separately; no equality of the singleton value with an adjacent value is asserted.

There are at most as many breakpoints as ordered observed treated-control pairs, and hence
\[
|\mathcal B(a)|\le n^2.
\]
If \(b=|\mathcal B(a)|\), the line is partitioned into \(b+1\) open components and \(b\) singleton breakpoints.  The definition of \(\mathsf{Invert}\), together with the exactness of \(\mathsf{ChamberMax}\), therefore reconstructs
\[
\mathcal I_\alpha(a)=\{\delta:P_\delta(a)>\alpha\}
\]
as the union of precisely the accepted open components and accepted singleton breakpoints, using \(2b+1=O(n^2)\) calls.  This gives exact endpoint inclusion even when the set is disconnected.  Finally, if the schedule has a true common additive effect \(\delta\), finite-sample validity gives
\(\Pr_w\{\delta\in\mathcal I_\alpha(A)\}\ge1-\alpha\); the inversion calculation itself makes no monotonicity or connectedness assumption.
